ESV.1: There was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim of the hill country of Ephraim whose name was Elkanah the son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, an Ephrathite.
ESV.2: He had two wives. The name of the one was Hannah, and the name of the other, Peninnah. And Peninnah had children, but Hannah had no children.
ESV.3: Now this man used to go up year by year from his city to worship and to sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh, where the two sons of Eli, Hophni and Phinehas, were priests of the LORD.
ESV.4: On the day when Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions to Peninnah his wife and to all her sons and daughters.
ESV.5: But to Hannah he gave a double portion, because he loved her, though the LORD had closed her womb.
ESV.6: And her rival used to provoke her grievously to irritate her, because the LORD had closed her womb.
ESV.7: So it went on year by year. As often as she went up to the house of the LORD, she used to provoke her. Therefore Hannah wept and would not eat.
ESV.8: And Elkanah, her husband, said to her, “Hannah, why do you weep? And why do you not eat? And why is your heart sad? Am I not more to you than ten sons?”
ESV.9: After they had eaten and drunk in Shiloh, Hannah rose. Now Eli the priest was sitting on the seat beside the doorpost of the temple of the LORD.
ESV.10: She was deeply distressed and prayed to the LORD and wept bitterly.
ESV.11: And she vowed a vow and said, “O LORD of hosts, if you will indeed look on the affliction of your servant and remember me and not forget your servant, but will give to your servant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life, and no razor shall touch his head.”
ESV.12: As she continued praying before the LORD, Eli observed her mouth.
ESV.13: Hannah was speaking in her heart; only her lips moved, and her voice was not heard. Therefore Eli took her to be a drunken woman.
ESV.14: And Eli said to her, “How long will you go on being drunk? Put your wine away from you.”
ESV.15: But Hannah answered, “No, my lord, I am a woman troubled in spirit. I have drunk neither wine nor strong drink, but I have been pouring out my soul before the LORD.
ESV.16: Do not regard your servant as a worthless woman, for all along I have been speaking out of my great anxiety and vexation.”
ESV.17: Then Eli answered, “Go in peace, and the God of Israel grant your petition that you have made to him.”
ESV.18: And she said, “Let your servant find favor in your eyes.” Then the woman went her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.
ESV.19: They rose early in the morning and worshiped before the LORD; then they went back to their house at Ramah. And Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her.
ESV.20: And in due time Hannah conceived and bore a son, and she called his name Samuel, for she said, “I have asked for him from the LORD.”
ESV.21: The man Elkanah and all his house went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and to pay his vow.
ESV.22: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, “As soon as the child is weaned, I will bring him, so that he may appear in the presence of the LORD and dwell there forever.”
ESV.23: Elkanah her husband said to her, “Do what seems best to you; wait until you have weaned him; only, may the LORD establish his word.” So the woman remained and nursed her son until she weaned him.
ESV.24: And when she had weaned him, she took him up with her, along with a three-year-old bull,  an ephah  of flour, and a skin of wine, and she brought him to the house of the LORD at Shiloh. And the child was young.
ESV.25: Then they slaughtered the bull, and they brought the child to Eli.
ESV.26: And she said, “Oh, my lord! As you live, my lord, I am the woman who was standing here in your presence, praying to the LORD.
ESV.27: For this child I prayed, and the LORD has granted me my petition that I made to him.
ESV.28: Therefore I have lent him to the LORD. As long as he lives, he is lent to the LORD.” And he worshiped the LORD there.

AMP.1: There was a certain man of Ramathaim-zophim, of the hill country of Ephraim, named Elkanah the son of Jeroham, the son of Elihu, the son of Tohu, the son of Zuph, an Ephraimite.
AMP.2: He had two wives, one named Hannah and the other named Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah had none.
AMP.3: This man went up from his city each year to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of hosts at Shiloh. Hophni and Phinehas, the two sons of Eli, were priests to the LORD there.
AMP.4: When the day came that Elkanah sacrificed, he would give portions [of the sacrificial meat] to Peninnah his wife and all her sons and daughters.
AMP.5: But to Hannah he would give a double portion, because he loved Hannah, but the LORD had given her no children.
AMP.6: Hannah's rival provoked her bitterly, to irritate and embarrass her, because the LORD had left her childless.
AMP.7: So it happened year after year, whenever she went up to the house of the LORD, Peninnah provoked her; so she wept and would not eat.
AMP.8: Then Elkanah her husband said to her, "Hannah, why do you cry and why do you not eat? Why are you so sad and discontent? Am I not better to you than ten sons?"
AMP.9: So Hannah got up after eating and drinking in Shiloh. Now Eli the priest was sitting on his seat beside the doorpost of the temple (tabernacle) of the LORD.
AMP.10: Hannah was greatly distressed, and she prayed to the LORD and wept in anguish.
AMP.11: She made a vow, saying, "O LORD of hosts, if You will indeed look on the affliction (suffering) of Your maidservant and remember, and not forget Your maidservant, but will give Your maidservant a son, then I will give him to the LORD all the days of his life; a razor shall never touch his head."
AMP.12: Now it happened as she continued praying before the LORD, that Eli was watching her mouth.
AMP.13: Hannah was speaking in her heart (mind); only her lips were moving, and her voice was not heard, so Eli thought she was drunk.
AMP.14: Eli said to her, "How long will you make yourself drunk? Get rid of your wine."
AMP.15: But Hannah answered, "No, my lord, I am a woman with a despairing spirit. I have not been drinking wine or any intoxicating drink, but I have poured out my soul before the LORD.
AMP.16: Do not regard your maidservant as a wicked and worthless woman, for I have spoken until now out of my great concern and [bitter] provocation."
AMP.17: Then Eli answered and said, "Go in peace; and may the God of Israel grant your petition that you have asked of Him."
AMP.18: Hannah said, "Let your maidservant find grace and favor in your sight." So the woman went on her way and ate, and her face was no longer sad.
AMP.19: The family got up early the next morning, worshiped before the LORD, and returned to their home in Ramah. Elkanah knew Hannah his wife, and the LORD remembered her [prayer].
AMP.20: It came about in due time, after Hannah had conceived, that she gave birth to a son; she named him Samuel, saying, "Because I have asked for him from the LORD."
AMP.21: Then the man Elkanah and all his household went up to offer to the LORD the yearly sacrifice and pay his vow.
AMP.22: But Hannah did not go up, for she said to her husband, "I will not go up until the child is weaned; and then I will bring him, so that he may appear before the LORD and remain there as long as he lives."

NLT.1: There was a man named Elkanah who lived in Ramah in the region of Zuph in the hill country of Ephraim. He was the son of Jeroham, son of Elihu, son of Tohu, son of Zuph, of Ephraim.
NLT.2: Elkanah had two wives, Hannah and Peninnah. Peninnah had children, but Hannah did not.
NLT.3: Each year Elkanah would travel to Shiloh to worship and sacrifice to the LORD of Heaven’s Armies at the Tabernacle. The priests of the LORD at that time were the two sons of Eli — Hophni and Phinehas.
NLT.4: On the days Elkanah presented his sacrifice, he would give portions of the meat to Peninnah and each of her children.
NLT.5: And though he loved Hannah, he would give her only one choice portion because the LORD had given her no children.
NLT.6: So Peninnah would taunt Hannah and make fun of her because the LORD had kept her from having children.
NLT.7: Year after year it was the same — Peninnah would taunt Hannah as they went to the Tabernacle. Each time, Hannah would be reduced to tears and would not even eat.
NLT.8: “Why are you crying, Hannah?” Elkanah would ask. “Why aren’t you eating? Why be downhearted just because you have no children? You have me — isn’t that better than having ten sons?”
NLT.9: Once after a sacrificial meal at Shiloh, Hannah got up and went to pray. Eli the priest was sitting at his customary place beside the entrance of the Tabernacle.
NLT.10: Hannah was in deep anguish, crying bitterly as she prayed to the LORD.
NLT.11: And she made this vow: “O LORD of Heaven’s Armies, if you will look upon my sorrow and answer my prayer and give me a son, then I will give him back to you. He will be yours for his entire lifetime, and as a sign that he has been dedicated to the LORD, his hair will never be cut. ”
NLT.12: As she was praying to the LORD, Eli watched her.
NLT.13: Seeing her lips moving but hearing no sound, he thought she had been drinking.
NLT.14: “Must you come here drunk?” he demanded. “Throw away your wine!”
NLT.15: “Oh no, sir!” she replied. “I haven’t been drinking wine or anything stronger. But I am very discouraged, and I was pouring out my heart to the LORD.
NLT.16: Don’t think I am a wicked woman! For I have been praying out of great anguish and sorrow.”
NLT.17: “In that case,” Eli said, “go in peace! May the God of Israel grant the request you have asked of him.”
NLT.18: “Oh, thank you, sir!” she exclaimed. Then she went back and began to eat again, and she was no longer sad.
NLT.19: The entire family got up early the next morning and went to worship the LORD once more. Then they returned home to Ramah. When Elkanah slept with Hannah, the LORD remembered her plea,
NLT.20: and in due time she gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, for she said, “I asked the LORD for him.”
NLT.21: The next year Elkanah and his family went on their annual trip to offer a sacrifice to the LORD and to keep his vow.
NLT.22: But Hannah did not go. She told her husband, “Wait until the boy is weaned. Then I will take him to the Tabernacle and leave him there with the LORD permanently. ”
NLT.23: “Whatever you think is best,” Elkanah agreed. “Stay here for now, and may the LORD help you keep your promise. ” So she stayed home and nursed the boy until he was weaned.
NLT.24: When the child was weaned, Hannah took him to the Tabernacle in Shiloh. They brought along a three-year-old bull for the sacrifice and a basket of flour and some wine.
NLT.25: After sacrificing the bull, they brought the boy to Eli.
NLT.26: “Sir, do you remember me?” Hannah asked. “I am the very woman who stood here several years ago praying to the LORD.
NLT.27: I asked the LORD to give me this boy, and he has granted my request.
NLT.28: Now I am giving him to the LORD, and he will belong to the LORD his whole life.” And they worshiped the LORD there.

MSG.1: There once was a man who lived in Ramathaim. He was descended from the old Zuph family in the Ephraim hills. His name was Elkanah. (He was connected with the Zuphs from Ephraim through his father Jeroham, his grandfather Elihu, and his great-grandfather Tohu.)
MSG.2: He had two wives. The first was Hannah; the second was Peninnah. Peninnah had children; Hannah did not.
MSG.3: Every year this man went from his hometown up to Shiloh to worship and offer a sacrifice to God-of-the-Angel-Armies. Eli and his two sons, Hophni and Phinehas, served as the priests of God there.
MSG.4: When Elkanah sacrificed, he passed helpings from the sacrificial meal around to his wife Peninnah and all her children,
MSG.5: but he always gave an especially generous helping to Hannah because he loved her so much, and because God had not given her children.
MSG.6: But her rival wife taunted her cruelly, rubbing it in and never letting her forget that God had not given her children.
MSG.7: This went on year after year. Every time she went to the sanctuary of God she could expect to be taunted. Hannah was reduced to tears and had no appetite.
MSG.8: Her husband Elkanah said, "Oh, Hannah, why are you crying? Why aren't you eating? And why are you so upset? Am I not of more worth to you than ten sons?"
MSG.9: So Hannah ate. Then she pulled herself together, slipped away quietly, and entered the sanctuary. The priest Eli was on duty at the entrance to God's Temple in the customary seat.
MSG.10: Crushed in soul, Hannah prayed to God and cried and cried—inconsolably.
MSG.11:
Then she made a vow:
Oh, God-of-the-Angel-Armies,
If you'll take a good, hard look at my pain,
If you'll quit neglecting me and go into action for me
By giving me a son,
I'll give him completely, unreservedly to you.
I'll set him apart for a life of holy discipline.
MSG.12: It so happened that as she continued in prayer before God, Eli was watching her closely.
MSG.13: Hannah was praying in her heart, silently. Her lips moved, but no sound was heard. Eli jumped to the conclusion that she was drunk.
MSG.14: He approached her and said, "You're drunk! How long do you plan to keep this up? Sober up, woman!"
MSG.15: Hannah said, "Oh no, sir—please! I'm a woman hard used. I haven't been drinking. Not a drop of wine or beer. The only thing I've been pouring out is my heart, pouring it out to God.

MSG.17: Eli answered her, "Go in peace. And may the God of Israel give you what you have asked of him."
MSG.18: "Think well of me—and pray for me!" she said, and went her way. Then she ate heartily, her face radiant.

MSG.22: Hannah didn't go. She told her husband, "After the child is weaned, I'll bring him myself and present him before God—and that's where he'll stay, for good."
MSG.23:

MSG.24: Then she took him up to Shiloh, bringing also the makings of a generous sacrificial meal—a prize bull, flour, and wine. The child was so young to be sent off!

MSG.26: Hannah said, "Excuse me, sir. Would you believe that I'm the very woman who was standing before you at this very spot, praying to God?

NIV.9: Once when they had finished eating and drinking in Shiloh, Hannah stood up. Now Eli the priest was sitting on a chair by the doorpost of the Lord’s temple.
NIV.10: In bitterness of soul Hannah wept much and prayed to the Lord.
NIV.11: And she made a vow, saying, “O Lord Almighty, if you will only look upon your servant’s misery and remember me, and not forget your servant but give her a son, then I will give him to the Lord for all the days of his life, and no razor will ever be used on his head.”
NIV.12: As she kept on praying to the Lord, Eli observed her mouth.
NIV.13: Hannah was praying in her heart, and her lips were moving but her voice was not heard. Eli thought she was drunk
NIV.14: and said to her, “How long will you keep on getting drunk? Get rid of your wine.”
NIV.15: “Not so, my lord,” Hannah replied, “I am a woman who is deeply troubled. I have not been drinking wine or beer; I was pouring out my soul to the Lord.
NIV.16: Do not take your servant for a wicked woman; I have been praying here out of my great anguish and grief.”
NIV.17: Eli answered, “Go in peace, and may the God of Israel grant you what you have asked of him.”
NIV.18: She said, “May your servant find favor in your eyes.” Then she went her way and ate something, and her face was no longer downcast.
NIV.19: Early the next morning they arose and worshiped before the Lord and then went back to their home at Ramah. Elkanah lay with Hannah his wife, and the Lord remembered her.
NIV.20: So in the course of time Hannah conceived and gave birth to a son. She named him Samuel, saying, “Because I asked the Lord for him.”
NIV.21:
Hannah Dedicates Samuel
When the man Elkanah went up with all his family to offer the annual sacrifice to the Lord and to fulfill his vow,
NIV.22: Hannah did not go. She said to her husband, “After the boy is weaned, I will take him and present him before the Lord, and he will live there always.”
NIV.23: “Do what seems best to you,” Elkanah her husband told her. “Stay here until you have weaned him; only may the Lord make good his word.” So the woman stayed at home and nursed her son until she had weaned him.
NIV.24: After he was weaned, she took the boy with her, young as he was, along with a three-year-old bull, an ephah of flour and a skin of wine, and brought him to the house of the Lord at Shiloh.
NIV.25: When they had slaughtered the bull, they brought the boy to Eli,
NIV.26: and she said to him, “As surely as you live, my lord, I am the woman who stood here beside you praying to the Lord.
NIV.27: I prayed for this child, and the Lord has granted me what I asked of him.
NIV.28: So now I give him to the Lord. For his whole life he will be given over to the Lord.” And he worshiped the Lord there.
